comments.content: I'll look into it tomorrow as I may have caused it with the refactor but I didn't touch the issue fetching or context window logic but either way I'll resolve whatever the issue is if not resolved by then

It looks like `/ask` is not working as it should be
1. Hallucinating against the spec because it never pulled the spec in.
2. The README inside the conversation block without distinction makes it appear as if it's part of the current conversation which also should state Pull Request in the header but appears as Issue
3. It looks like it hasn't pulled in the PR diff at all
Please see this [run](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-ask/actions/runs/11605147726/job/32315045572)
_related [context](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/permit-generation/pull/96#issuecomment-2448904538)_

Resolves #26
- returned hash matching for inter-repo references (cause of the original context). I can't actually QA the OG ctx issue because it's a hash match problem so my results would be different, but you'll see that's the problem if you edit the body
- fixed context window structure: correct headers, READMEs own section, and diff own section
- refactored PR and diff parsing using a combination of simple heuristic and encoding
- removing the largest of files from the context window and maxing our token limit as best we can
- optimized `promise.all()` usage and removed `github-diff-tool`
- hardcoded model token limits to help calcs, no endpoint afaik to pull this on the fly
- removed jsdoc and added helpful comments (we don't use JSDOC comments and I've been warned before)
- created an exhaustive list of extensions (using gpt) that we should automatically ignore and not even consider towards the goal of execution speed in large PRs to minimize encoding which is costly
- optimized diff parsing by splitting it into `per-file-diffs` because working down the way takes too long
- improved logs so we can see the full systemMessage as well as just the formatted chat 
QA: https://github.com/ubq-testing/ask-plugin/actions/runs/11620710161/job/32363062027
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c32f761-dd58-4b07-8567-caba4b967e1e)
You can inspect the action logs and see the structure, diff parsing and logs regarding what files were excluded from the diff etc.

I implemented your suggested strategy mate. This is a move towards improving exec speed by ignoring files outright that are not readable. 
Files are added to the diff smallest first but we auto exclude files that are blatantly over the model's limit as well as files that would not be comprehendible.
In my testing, encoding was a bottleneck so I tried to improve the speed as much as I could by removing anything that we shouldn't encode and making what we do encode smaller.
---
If it's unclear via code review what's happening I can produce a bunch internal logs and it can be inspected

empty strings are safe in this context. "" evaluates to null and if added into the context window it's nothing. The alternative means explicitly typing null and then filtering, wasn't sure which was cleaner.
I'll remove them and use the Octokit defined types which include `undefined | null` etc by default for this value
I've used in a few of my plugins now and yeah far more readable
removed it but if you think it's a good idea we can always return it

You should run it and QA it properly but files are not fetched. The single PR diff is split into sections based on the file sections included within the raw diff as per the regex used to split the diff.
It's an action, we have 6 hours and no cap I'm aware of in terms of memory, but this processes things fast, which was my intention considering how slow it can be to encode thousands of lines of diff, I know this by experimenting with various methods.
That raises the API calls and needs promise.all refactoring. My approach literally uses just the diff of the PR. 
Why fetch any files at all, we only send the diff not the full file, the diff is what's been changed within the file not the whole thing so why would we use the full file sizes that also raising api calls in the process and needs additional math logic to calculate differences etc - It makes sense to just use the diff.

Maybe it's best I close this PR
1. It involves quite a lot of changes that may or may not clash with your refactoring and vision for how things should work, as I appear to be stepping wrong no matter what it seems.
2. I feel my opinions and work is repeatedly being dismissed without proper QA or review and it's feeling combative, and I'm not vying for ownership of this plugin. I did write and rewrite it three times for V1 and V2 so I felt a sense of ownership to it but I'm happy to step back and get out of your way with things. I can focus on other areas of development no problem.
3. I'm happy to help if requested but I think you and 0x4007 have got things more than covered.
Please feel free to close the PR or take over it again, no hard feelings or anything, I just don't want any tension with anyone in the org that's all.

I QA'd using the original issue which caused the failure due to including `/dist`.
In my debugging the gql fetch was erroring out and doing nothing pretty much. Although I was testing on my own issue with the body as the original error issue, all context was coming in without it. Maybe I've overlooked something but I've removed it since it's unused.

@sshivaditya2019 @0x4007 @gentlementlegen 
ready for review

1. First we split each file in the diff into sections
2. Then we determine quickly if it's above the models limit by `diff.length / 3.5`
3. We mark files to be added to the diff via `usedTokens + approximation < tokensRemaining`
4. Binary, bundles, etc they are the first to be excluded before any encoding as they tend to overshoot the model limit.
5. We mark the smallest files to be added first building up to the biggest (minus any that outright overshoot)
6. We get an accurate encoding of the sections and start popping the largest.
7. We return the included files.
I think this is pretty efficient and fits the purpose well. I tried an alternative, which was use the gitTree and base it on `file.size` but it wasn't as efficient or effective.
I'm unaware of any packages but I think a simple file ext system would be as good as we'd need it to be. An alt approach is feed an array of the filenames to GPT and have it determine which to exclude but seems redundant. I can look into packages if my approach isn't effective/accepted for merge.
@sshivaditya @sshivaditya2019 @gentlementlegen please review when you can

[As a rough rule of thumb, 1 token is approximately 4 characters or 0.75 words for English text.](https://platform.openai.com/docs/concepts/tokens#tokens)
A rough approximation of OpenAIs encoding

I [do use](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-ask/pull/28/files#diff-23c426746bbf7449570050410ae6fa234caedd116e8b2f1e7fa82e1bbc1e7577R42) the official tokenizer for a more accurate reading once I've excluded the files that are clearly over the limit with the quick approximation, such as dist files etc. Encoding those massive files is a terrible bottleneck and should be avoided if possible in my opinion, which is why I've implemented things the way I have.
I calculate `tokensRemaining` at the beginning via `model.maxTokens - model.maxOutput` which gives us full response windows

I'm finished with it so if that's your review done you can merge it I guess
Our dist builds range from 3MB-16MB, encoding these takes a lot of time especially the larger ones which was the one I used for development. Partners may have much larger files. dist files are added via a workflow (for us) and it tends to change huge sections, potentially the entire file in git's eyes.
The primary optimization was reducing API calls to maintain speed in building the ctx window, which includes encoding the diff. 
- Encoding the full thing and slicing then re-encoding takes too long: we don't have file sizes to selectively slice without encoding each section or spamming the API.
- Say we use `perFileDiff.length` encoding and then adding to the returned diff til we hit a 15MB file which will never fit, but we'd need to encode it unnecessarily to find out if it would
- In my testing the token count was around 35k I believe with the diff stripped so we have a huge amount of tokens left to use but the 15MB file never had a chance in of being included
- `promise.all` usage was implemented to improve exec speed building the ctx window, hitting the secondary was either a reduce speed or reduce calls problem.
- I chose reduce calls, but introduced a bottleneck encoding the entire diff so further optimizations had to be made and so it made sense to stay inline with OpenAIs rule of thumb for their encoder but not perform a full encoding of 16MB worth of code when not required
I'm pretty intentional in my work there's not something I'll do 'just because', for no reason or to show off or something whatever the opinion might me.
Feel free to ask why I did something in particular if you are unclear of why I did it, I'm happy to explain my thought process if it's not clear via review alone.
I'm happy to remove anything that you guys don't want or don't think is required and we'll get this merged ASAP

comments.content:
Are we pulling in all the diffs? I'm not sure that's efficient. We’re processing a file with thousands of lines when we could have just made another Octokit call, as the library was doing. With that call, we could get statistics and then pull files based on their diff size. I don't think it's worth saving one or more Octokit calls at the expense of increased memory usage and processing time.
A better approach would be to compare the commit hashes and check the file sizes between them, fetching files selectively instead of the current method.
Got it, that clarifies the implementation. I thought actions were restricted to 500MB.

I really appreciate your work on this PR and want to encourage you to continue with it. I don’t have any issues with the changes you’ve made. The refactoring is still a work in progress, as you can see in the draft PR, so we can definitely work together to align everything.
